reason: The evidence is wrong about its own book, but the citation on the card is right and I verified it another way, so the line stands. The evidence calls Project Gutenberg 16950 “the Macmillan collected volume”. It is not: I downloaded it and its front matter reads “The World’s Classics CLXXXIV … Humphrey Milford, Oxford University Press”, with the note that the contents of the two books “were first published in one volume in 1913”. So the verifier read an Oxford reprint while naming Macmillan. Rather than trust it, I went to the first edition itself: the Wikisource transcription of Page:Goblin Market and Other Poems - C G Rossetti (1862, 1st ed).djvu/144, which gives the poem under the heading UP-HILL as “Does the road wind up-hill all the way? / Yes, to the very end. / Will the day’s journey take the whole long day? / From morn to night, my friend.” That is the quotation word for word, hyphen in “up-hill” and all, in the edition the card names. The Oxford reprint agrees with it, and carries a printed line number 10 against “Those who have gone before”, which independently fixes the quoted stanza as lines 1 to 4. Attribution right and never in doubt; no speaker, since the poem is an unattributed question-and-answer and the card does not pretend otherwise. Locator right, and the first-publication history in the proposal (Macmillan’s Magazine, February 1861, then the 1862 book) is accurate, with the card sensibly citing the book. In scope: 1862, a named poem in a named collection, no scripture, no translation to drift. Publishable, and the bleakness test passes on the quoted stanza: the allegory ends at an inn with “beds for all who come”, not in the dark, and these four lines read as steadiness rather than gloom. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Rossetti 0 of 3, not banned, once in the month. Source leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote, 90 characters; tag Poetry is the form. The only repair needed is in the evidence field, which should name the 1862 first-edition scan or the Oxford World’s Classics 1913 reprint it actually read, not Macmillan.
